jobs.jd_full:
Upwork Inc.'s (Nasdaq: UPWK) family of companies connects businesses with global, AI-enabled talent across every contingent work type including freelance, fractional, and payrolled. This portfolio includes the Upwork Marketplace, which connects businesses with on-demand access to highly skilled talent across the globe, and Lifted, which provides a purpose-built solution for enterprise organizations to source, contract, manage, and pay talent across the full spectrum of contingent work. From Fortune 100 enterprises to entrepreneurs, businesses rely on Upwork Inc. to find and hire expert talent, leverage AI-powered work solutions, and drive business transformation. With access to professionals spanning more than 10,000 skills across AI & machine learning, software development, sales & marketing, customer support, finance & accounting, and more, the Upwork family of companies enables businesses of all sizes to scale, innovate, and transform their workforces for the age of AI and beyond.

Since its founding, Upwork Inc. has facilitated more than $30 billion in total transactions and services as it fulfills its purpose to create opportunity in every era of work. Learn more about the Upwork Marketplace at Upwork.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and X; and learn more about Lifted at Go-Lifted and follow on LinkedIn.

About the Role

Upwork's COO and GM of Marketplace operates across one of the broadest organizational portfolios in the company - spanning Legal, Information Security, Marketing, Payments, Trust & Safety, Communications, Customer Support, Design, and Product. The Chief of Staff to the COO exists to make that model work: not as a coordinator, but as a true operating partner who extends the COO's capacity, sharpens decision-making, and holds together a complex, fast-moving organization.

This role requires someone who has earned the confidence to walk into any room, speak with authority, and immediately earn credibility - with the COO's direct reports, with the executive team, and with external stakeholders. It is a senior, strategic seat, and will be treated as one.

What You'll Do

Strategic Partnership

Serve as a trusted thought partner - not as a gatekeeper, but as someone who makes every interaction with the COO more valuable. You will be the person the COO thinks out loud with, who surfaces risks before they become problems, and who ensures decisions are grounded in the right data and framing. You will push back privately, represent the COO's point of view publicly, and discern between the two like it was remembering to breathe.

Prepare the COO for high-stakes conversations - drafting and driving board presentations, executive reviews, cross-functional negotiations - surfacing not just what is known, but what remains ambiguous or contested. Where there's a decision to be made, you'll come with options and a point of view, not just a summary.

Operational Integration

Own the operating rhythm of the COO organization. Monthly and quarterly business reviews, annual planning cycles, leadership forums - you will ensure these are substantive, efficient, and connected to strategic priorities rather than calendar obligations. You'll work directly with finance and functional leads to ensure budget is managed with discipline and that trade-off decisions are made proactively, not reactively.

Across a portfolio this wide, fragmentation is the enemy. You will identify where alignment is breaking down, where decisions are falling through the cracks, and where accountability needs to be reinforced - and you will fix those things without waiting to be asked.

Execution and Clarity

Maintain a clear line of sight across key initiatives and ensure the COO has the information, context, and preparation needed to drive outcomes - not just attend meetings. You will own the quality of materials that come to the COO, provide direct feedback to senior leaders preparing those materials, and ensure that executive time is protected for the work that only the COO can do.

When cross-functional friction stalls something important, you will unblock it. You will know when to convene the right people, when to clarify decision rights, and when to escalate versus resolve.

Culture and Continuity

Model the leadership values Upwork expects of its people. Be the connective tissue between strategy and execution - translating intent into direction for a team that operates across remarkably diverse functions. During transitions or periods of organizational change, be the source of stability and continuity.

What You Bring

You have operated at the intersection of strategy and execution in a high-velocity environment - consulting, investment banking, a high-growth tech company, or some combination. You understand how businesses work, how organizations behave under pressure, and how to move complex stakeholders without formal authority.

You are organized in a way that others notice. Not in a process-for-process's-sake way, but in a way that instills confidence: things don't fall through the cracks around you, and the people you work with know it. You think clearly under ambiguity, write and communicate with precision, and can build a compelling deck and the strategy behind it in the same sitting.

You have the discretion and judgement to be a confidant - discreet with sensitive information, frank in private, and diplomatically effective in every other setting. You know when to be direct and when to be patient. You don't need credit, but you do need to be trusted, and you earn that trust by consistently being great at your job and consistently acting with integrity.

10+ years of relevant experience; MBA or equivalent strongly preferred. Prior Chief of Staff experience or a similar senior operating role is a plus, but the profile matters more than the title.

Come change how the world works.

At Upwork, you’ll shape the future of work for a global, remote-first workforce, creating economic opportunities for professionals worldwide. While we have a physical office in Palo Alto, we currently hire full-time employees in 34 U.S. states, making it easier than ever to join our mission from wherever you call home.

Our culture is built on trust, risk-taking, customer focus, and excellence, all in service of our core mission: to create economic opportunities so people have better lives. We embrace authenticity and inclusion, encouraging everyone to bring their whole selves to work. Personal and professional growth is a priority here, supported through development programs, mentorship, and our Upwork Belonging Communities.

We’re proud to offer benefits that go beyond the basics, including comprehensive medical coverage for you and your family, unlimited PTO, a 401(k) plan with matching, 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Visit our Life at Upwork page to learn more about our values, working principles, and the overall employee experience.

About Us:

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.

The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Business AI Operations Specialist to help Spreedly transform how business teams operate by identifying high-value opportunities and translating them into practical, scalable AI-enabled workflows.

This role leads AI workflow discovery across R&D and builds prioritized solutions across R&D and other business functions. It also owns key Marketing Operations activities outside of scoring, routing, and analytics, which are managed by Revenue Operations.

The ideal candidate combines strong operational judgment with hands-on implementation skills. They can understand how work happens today, identify opportunities for meaningful improvement, and deliver practical solutions that teams adopt and continue to use.

Success in this role will be measured by the on-time delivery of prioritized workflows, improved operational efficiency, strong adoption, measurable business outcomes, and reliable processes and solutions.

Responsibilities:

R&D Workflow Discovery

  • Lead AI workflow discovery across Product, Engineering, and other R&D functions.
  • Partner with stakeholders to understand business needs, operational challenges, and existing processes.
  • Identify opportunities where AI and automation can reduce manual work, improve execution, or increase productivity.
  • Document and maintain identified R&D opportunities in the shared company AI workflow inventory for prioritization.
  • Translate selected opportunities into clear requirements, success measures, and implementation plans.

Business AI Execution

  • Design and build prioritized AI workflows across R&D and other business functions.
  • Translate business requirements into practical solutions using approved AI platforms and shared capabilities.
  • Deliver assigned solutions on time and communicate risks or delays early.
  • Focus primarily on operational AI workflows that can deliver measurable business value.
  • Test solutions with business users, incorporate feedback, and support successful adoption.
  • Partner with the AI Enablement & Solutions Lead when initiatives require advanced architecture, reusable capabilities, or complex cross-functional design.
  • Apply shared AI standards and recommended implementation patterns to assigned solutions.

Solution Ownership

  • Serve as the AI build owner for assigned workflows.
  • Own solution design, development, testing, launch, maintenance, and ongoing optimization.
  • Partner with internal business customers to validate requirements, support adoption, and measure business outcomes.
  • Develop documentation, user guidance, and training materials for delivered solutions.
  • Monitor solution performance and identify opportunities for continued improvement.
  • Ensure assigned workflows remain aligned with shared AI standards and company priorities.

Marketing Operations

  • Own Marketing Operations activities outside of scoring, routing, and analytics.
  • Manage campaign operations and configuration, nurture programs, audience segmentation, webinars, and marketing automation.
  • Support data quality, source management, auditing, lead-flow execution, and operational governance in partnership with Revenue Operations.
  • Optimize the marketing technology stack, including HubSpot, Salesforce, Influ2, and related platforms.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations on processes and systems involving scoring, routing, analytics, and reporting.
  • Ensure Marketing Operations processes and workflows remain scalable, reliable, and well maintained.

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience in Business Operations, Marketing Operations, process improvement, automation, or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and maintaining operational workflows.
  • Experience using Claude or similar tools to build AI-enabled business workflows.
  • Experience with APIs, low-code or no-code platforms, workflow automation, or prompt engineering.
  • Experience applying AI or automation to improve business processes and productivity.
  • Strong ability to translate business needs into practical, usable solutions.
  • Experience with business systems, workflow automation, and modern technology platforms.
  • Experience with HubSpot, Salesforce, or comparable business platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive adoption and organizational change without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical, project-management, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across different business functions.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to reliable, maintainable execution.

Additional Skills We Value:

  • Experience with n8n, Apollo, Clay, Influ2, or similar platforms.
  • Experience supporting Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, or Revenue Operations.
  • Experience with SQL, reporting, analytics, or data visualization.
  • Experience in SaaS, fintech, payments, or another technology environment.
  • Experience supporting AI workflow discovery or business process redesign.

We Offer Our US-Based Employees:

  • Competitive salary + Equity
  • Outstanding Medical and Dental benefits, including 100% employer-paid options
  • Company-paid Life and Disability insurance
  • Optional vision and supplemental insurance options, and various Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
  • Open Paid Time Off policy + 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents

Spreedly Product Offering:

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:

Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
About Us:

Future is building a personalized guidance system for lifelong health. We help people understand what to do next for their body, goals, and stage of life — then support them in turning those decisions into sustained behavior change. By combining AI, human expertise, personal health data, and accountability, Future helps members improve performance today while building the resilience, capacity, and healthspan they need for decades to come.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the core marketplace experience. We’re rethinking things from the ground up—you won’t be inheriting a roadmap, a backlog, or a set of conventions. You’ll be building the product from the ground up alongside the CPTO.

This role requires someone who thinks in systems. A marketplace is not a single product—it’s an ecosystem. You’ll need to hold the consumer experience, the practitioner experience, the matching logic, the trust and safety layer, the business model, and the growth loops in your head simultaneously, and make smart tradeoffs between them every day.

You will report directly to the CPTO and work alongside a small, senior engineering team. There are no layers between you and the work, and no layers between you and the decisions that shape the company.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

Product Strategy & Vision

  • Define the product vision and strategy for the marketplace, grounded in deep user understanding, competitive analysis, and a clear-eyed view of the business model.
  • Own the roadmap end-to-end. Decide what to build, what to kill, and what to sequence—with conviction, not consensus.
  • Develop and maintain a strong point of view on where the wellness and longevity market is heading and how our product should evolve to lead, not follow.
  • TRUE 0→1 product thinking: identify the fastest and cheapest ways to validate core assumptions before committing significant engineering investment.

Marketplace Systems Thinking

  • Design and optimize both sides of the marketplace: the consumer journey (discovery → trust → booking → retention) and the practitioner journey (onboarding → activation → growth → advocacy).
  • Develop frameworks for marketplace health: supply/demand balance, liquidity metrics, matching quality, and network effects.
  • Own the cold-start playbook. Figure out how to bootstrap supply and demand in new verticals and geographies.
  • Think critically about marketplace trust and safety—credential verification, reviews, dispute resolution—as a product surface, not an afterthought.

Execution & Shipping

  • Partner with engineering and design to ship continuously. Write clear, opinionated specs. Run structured discovery. Make scope decisions that keep velocity high.
  • Instrument everything. Define success metrics for every feature. Run experiments. Kill things that aren’t working.
  • Balance competing priorities across consumer, practitioner, and platform workstreams while maintaining a clear view of the overall system.

Business & Growth

  • Own the business logic of the marketplace: pricing models, take rates, subscription tiers, transaction economics.
  • Partner with growth and marketing on acquisition loops, activation funnels, and retention strategies for both sides of the marketplace.
  • Use data to identify the highest-leverage opportunities. Build the instrumentation and dashboards needed to operate with clarity.

AI as a Force Multiplier

  • AI should be part of your daily operating system as a product manager.
    • Research synthesis: distilling user interviews, market data, and competitive intel at speed.
    • Spec and strategy drafting: using AI to accelerate writing, then applying your judgment to sharpen it.
    • Data analysis: querying, visualizing, and interpreting data with AI assistance.
    • Prototyping: rapidly generating UI concepts, user flows, and copy variations.
    • Workflow automation: building personal and team workflows that eliminate toil.
  • Bring a perspective on how AI should be woven into the product itself—personalized recommendations, intelligent matching, automated practitioner tools.
  • Raise the AI fluency bar for the entire team. Share what’s working. Push others to adopt.

WHO YOU ARE:

Experience & Background

  • 7+ years of product management experience, with significant time on marketplace, platform, or multi-sided products.
  • You’ve been a startup founder, a founding PM, or an early employee who built 0→1 products with limited resources. You know what it’s like to ship when there’s no playbook, no established process, and no safety net.
  • You’ve operated at the Senior, Staff, or Principal level—or you’ve functioned at that altitude regardless of your title (common for founders and early-stage operators).
  • Proven ability to ship products that drive measurable business outcomes, not just features.

Domain Passion

You are passionate about wellness, longevity, and preventive health. This isn’t a box you’re checking—you have a personal connection to this space. Maybe you’ve seen the healthcare system fail someone you love. Maybe you’ve gone deep on your own health optimization. Maybe you’ve worked in healthtech and know firsthand how much better it could be.

You stay current on trends in functional medicine, longevity research, consumer health, and the evolving practitioner landscape.

Working Style

  • Exceptional product taste. You see what’s working, what’s not, and what’s missing—and you care about the details.
  • Clear, precise communicator—in writing, in specs, in conversation, and in a room with engineers.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and pace. You don’t need permission to act. You don’t wait for perfect information.
  • Strong analytical chops. You pull your own data, run your own analyses, and let evidence shape your decisions.
  • Low ego, high ownership. You do what needs to be done—whether that’s writing a spec, responding to a user complaint, or fixing a broken onboarding email.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Direct experience in health, wellness, longevity, or consumer health—and an understanding of the regulatory, trust, and compliance dynamics of the space.
  • Experience building or scaling a marketplace through cold-start, supply/demand balancing, and network effects.
  • Experience building AI-native products (not just AI features bolted onto existing workflows).
  • Technical depth—you can read code, write SQL, or prototype in no-code/low-code tools.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

We believe great people should be well paid and meaningfully invested in what they’re building. We hire individuals who raise the bar, and we compensate accordingly — with competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits designed to support your life and growth.

  • Base Compensation: $185,000-220,000 The salary range is set based on multiple considerations including business needs, market demands, talent availability, experience, and unique skills and attributes. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

  • Equity: Meaningful early-stage equity package with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff.

  • Health Coverage: All employees who meet the eligibility requirements receive Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus life and disability coverage

  • Retirement: 401(k) plan with tax-advantaged savings options

  • Remote-First: Work from anywhere in the continental U.S. We’re a distributed team that values async communication, deep focus time, and intentional in-person gatherings.

  • Home Office Support: Stipend to set up your workspace and monthly support for internet or coworking

  • Wellness: Monthly wellness stipend for fitness, recovery, and overall wellbeing, plus access to mental health resources and therapy support

  • Flexible Time Off: Flexible PTO so you can rest, recharge, and take care of life outside of work

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
About Bastion

Bastion provides the regulated infrastructure businesses need to hold, move, and issue stablecoins. Our platform combines custodial wallets, global payment orchestration, and stablecoin issuance. Customers can use each product independently or connect them into a single end-to-end flow.

We operate through our own regulated entities, with compliance and risk controls built directly into the platform. We can also support customers operating under their own licenses with the compliance and financial operations required to run their programs.

Overview

We are looking for a Product Manager to own our Shared Services vertical, the set of foundational capabilities that every other product area at Bastion depends on. You’ll turn ambiguous, compliance-heavy problems into clear, sequenced, shippable work. You’ll own the roadmap, requirements, compliance checkpoints, quality bar, and stakeholder communication for a vertical that gates customer commitments across the platform.

Shared Services sits where product, engineering, and compliance meet. Much of the work centers on the controls and obligations that make stablecoin infrastructure trustworthy: identity and due-diligence flows, third-party risk controls, regulatory reporting, and the policies that govern how money moves.

This is a high-leverage IC role with real ownership from week one. It may be up-leveled to Senior PM depending on the candidate and interview performance.

We are open to candidates anywhere in the United States, with an advantage for those in (or willing to relocate or travel often to) New York City.

No prior experience working with stablecoins is required. We have a preference for prior experience with fintech, compliance, or risk.

Work to Be Done

Instead of a list of requirements, we want to give you a directional look into the first 30, 90, and 180 days on the job.

We are a startup, so the pace is fast and the specific work will change. People who thrive here are finding ways to contribute in their first week, and fully productive in their third month.

If you think this is something you can handle, we will be excited to speak with you.

First 30 days: Learn the vertical AND take work off the table

  • Map the Shared Services surface area: the foundational capabilities other verticals depend on, their current state, and where delivery risk is concentrated

  • Meet your partners in Engineering, Compliance, and GTM; learn the escalation paths and how Shared Services work gates commitments elsewhere

  • Take ownership of requirements for at least one active compliance-critical workstream and turn it into clear, sequenced, engineer-ready specs

  • Stand up a lightweight triage cadence so incoming requirements and issues stop piling up

  • Ship or unblock visible progress on at least one customer-gating milestone

  • Outcomes

    • A clear picture of the Shared Services roadmap and how its items gate customer commitments

    • Partners know what you own and how to route work to you

    • At least one workstream materially advanced through sharper requirements and sequencing

By 90 days: Own the roadmap and run the cadence

  • Own the Shared Services roadmap end to end: themes, sequencing, milestones, and compliance checkpoints aligned to company priorities

  • Run a predictable operating rhythm (planning, triage, risk tracking, and stakeholder updates) that Engineering and Compliance can rely on

  • Drive requirements and delivery across several concurrent regulated workstreams, holding the quality bar on each

  • Partner with Compliance to define and track checkpoints that keep flows defensible without stalling delivery

  • Keep stakeholders across verticals current on status, risks, and tradeoffs for the items that gate their commitments

  • Outcomes

    • Shared Services has a clear, sequenced roadmap with defined compliance checkpoints

    • Delivery runs on a predictable cadence with proactive risk management

    • Measurable progress on the workstreams that gate customer commitments

By 180 days: Scale the vertical’s reliability

  • Sustain delivery across several regulated workstreams with the quality bar consistently met

  • Build the instrumentation and feedback loops that make prioritization and compliance tracking repeatable rather than ad hoc

  • Institutionalize the requirements, triage, and checkpoint practices so the vertical runs consistently as load grows

  • Anticipate upcoming regulatory and customer obligations and get ahead of them in the roadmap

  • Find ways to reduce recurring load on Engineering through better sequencing and reusable capability

  • Outcomes

    • Shared Services operates with repeatable processes and clear decision-making

    • Compliance checkpoints and quality bars are documented and consistently applied

    • Clear, measurable reduction in delivery ambiguity for the teams that depend on the vertical

Some challenges you might tackle

  • Turning open-ended compliance obligations (identity and due-diligence flows, third-party risk controls, regulatory reporting, travel-rule requirements) into clear, shippable product work

  • Sequencing a heavily loaded vertical so the highest-gating items land first

  • Reasoning clearly about stablecoin infrastructure (issuance, custody, settlement, and on-chain movement) to make sound product tradeoffs

  • Keeping a reliable triage and requirements cadence under a heavy, shifting workload

  • Creating clarity from ambiguity when obligations are incomplete or customer needs conflict
